source_refs.note: 1. Linear Polarization: a main subheading of 8.2 Types of polarization, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 176-176.

blocks.text: When the electric field vector oscillates in a single plane, light is said to be linearly polarized as shown in Fig.8.4 (a). Example is the light passing through a polarizing filter, like sunglasses.

blocks.alt: Axes x and x' (horizontal), y and y' (vertical) and z and z' (drawn in perspective) meet at O. A sine wave travels along x in the x-y plane; the half-waves above the axis are filled with magenta vertical lines and those below with cyan lines. Label: Space (3D).
blocks.caption: Figure 8.4 (a): Linear polarization of light (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.4 (a)).
